draft.title: Seasonal indices
card: A seasonal index shows how one season (such as a quarter, month or day) compares with the average season. An index of 1 means that season is average.
An index above 1 means the season is above average. An index of 1.2 means 20% above average. An index below 1 means below average, so 0.9 means 10% below average.
Over a full cycle, the seasonal indices add up to the number of seasons. With 4 quarters, the indices add to 4. With 12 months, they add to 12.
Example: if the indices for three quarters are 1.3, 0.8 and 1.1, the fourth must be 4 − (1.3 + 0.8 + 1.1) = 0.8.
draft.remember: Index 1 is average. Above 1 is above average. The indices add to the number of seasons.

a.q: A café in Geelong has a seasonal index of 0.85 for Mondays. What does this tell us about Monday sales?
a.why: An index of 0.85 is 1 − 0.85 = 0.15 below 1, so sales are 15% below average. Saying 85% below confuses the index with the size of the gap.

b.q: A pool in Mildura has quarterly seasonal indices of 1.45, 0.70 and 1.05 for three quarters. What is the seasonal index for the fourth quarter?
b.why: Four indices must add to 4. The three given add to 3.20, so the fourth is 4 − 3.20 = 0.80. Answering 1.00 wrongly assumes the missing index is average.
b.clue: How many quarters are there, and what must the indices add to?

problems.detail: The right answer (0.80) is the same as the missing index in the card's worked example (0.8), so a student could pick it from memory of the example without doing the subtraction. Changing the given indices would give a different fourth value.
